evidence.s1_requirements: snapshot() returns {version, definition, root} plain object (src/BehaviourTree.ts:131); TreeSnapshot/NodeSnapshot exported in src/index.ts; restore() validates then restores (BehaviourTree.ts:139-148); keeps node states, children, repeat/retry target+current counts (Repeat.ts:127-144, Retry.ts), lotto selectedChild index (Lotto.ts), wait totalDuration+waitedDuration (Wait.ts:111-138); wait restore sets initialUpdateTime = now - waited so offline time doesn't count, getDeltaTime mode keeps accumulated value; finished trees restore as finished; README snapshot()/restore(snapshot) section with realistic workflow example; version 4.4.0 in package.json, package-lock.json and Version History.
evidence.s1_correctness: Every stateful field found by grepping src/nodes (Lotto.selectedChild, Repeat/Retry counts, Wait times, Action promise fields) is saved; Node._guardPath is structural. Restore writes _state directly so no callbacks. Settled promise result stored as String(value), which reproduces the same error text since Action uses `${value}`. Node ids restored so getTreeNodeDetails matches. Stale promises ignored via updatePromise identity check (Action.ts:120-149, 214). Tests cover every composite/decorator at 0-4 steps, guards aborting, entry/exit callbacks not repeated, random counts/durations/lotto with differing random functions, wait remaining time in both modes, infinite delta time.
evidence.s2_validation: getDefinitionHash (BehaviourTreeSnapshot.ts:87-136) canonicalises sorted keys, args ??= [], succeedOnAbort for guards, sorted roots, then cyrb53; validateSnapshot throws "the snapshot does not match the tree's definition" (line 161), rejects null/array/non-object (148), missing definition, version, malformed nodes, all before mutating. Tests: MDSL<->JSON both directions incl. defaults omitted, whitespace/comments, differences in name/arg/duration/count/guard/weights rejected, tree unchanged after ~24 invalid inputs (spec 543-726). Pending promise saved as READY (Action.ts:195-197), tested with entry callback re-run; README documents limitation.
evidence.s3_fixes: Step 3 patch is test-only (diff/step3.patch); the step-2 code already satisfied both reports: Node.restore bypasses setState, getSnapshot builds fresh objects, Action.restore keeps a reference to the snapshot's updatePromiseResult but never mutates it. Regression tests added for no onNodeStateChange during restore, snapshot unaffected by stepping source/restored trees, snapshot-after-restore equality, including settled promise case. Residual: Wait.getSnapshot (Wait.ts:116-121) reads new Date() so in clock mode a snapshot taken >=1ms after restore differs from s; tests use sinon fake timers and hide this.
evidence.design: Each node class overrides getSnapshot/restore for its own state (Node, Composite, Decorator, Lotto, Repeat, Retry, Action, Wait) following the existing getDetails pattern. Weaknesses: NodeSnapshot is a single flat type with optional per-node fields rather than a discriminated union; validation is centralised in a type switch in BehaviourTreeSnapshot.ts:206 rather than owned by nodes; Node.uid lost readonly. Hash implemented locally without dependencies; minimal public API (snapshot, restore, two types).
evidence.tests: New test/BehaviourTreeSnapshot.spec.ts (~1080 lines) with mocha/chai/sinon; lockstep helper assertRestoredTreeMatches compares node details and agent call logs after JSON round trip; covers all node types, random choices, both wait modes, guards, callbacks, promises (pending/settled/rejected/stale), invalid input, definition matching, step 3 regressions. No existing tests modified. Minor: 'of a finished tree: restores as finished, and the next step runs the tree again' (spec:360) snapshots after 1 step with a running 100ms real-clock wait and asserts RUNNING, so it does not test a finished tree (the lotto test does).
evidence.docs: README adds snapshot() and restore(snapshot) sections with a correct fs-based workflow example, lists what is kept, wait timing, finished tree, no callbacks, error cases; step 2 adds MDSL/JSON equivalence, definition-mismatch error and the pending-promise limitation next to the API. Version History row 4.4.0 and package.json/package-lock.json bumped once (unreleased feature kept at 4.4.0 in later steps).
evidence.process: 15 commits with conventional, accurate messages (feat/fix/docs/build/test), dist regenerated in separate build commits matching the repo's tracked dist, step 3 honestly committed as test-only. No new dependencies, no unrequested features beyond node-id restoration needed for getTreeNodeDetails equality.

unmet_requirements: Step 3 report 2 (partly): a snapshot taken right after restore(s) is not guaranteed equal to s for a running wait node in clock mode, because Wait.getSnapshot recomputes elapsed time from new Date(); only verified under fake timers.
strengths: Snapshot and restore cover every node type and stateful field, including settled promise results, guards, random choices and both wait time modes, and validation completes before any change.
Definition matching via a canonical hash correctly treats MDSL and hand-written JSON as the same, tested in both directions and against many near-miss definitions.
Thorough lockstep test suite plus clear README docs, the limitation note and correct versioning.
issues: Clock-mode wait snapshots depend on the current time, so a snapshot taken right after restore(s) with a real clock can differ from s; the step 3 tests hide this with fake timers.
NodeSnapshot is one loose type with optional per-node fields, and validation is centralised in a type switch instead of being owned by each node.
The 'of a finished tree … runs the tree again' test never snapshots a finished tree (it snapshots mid-wait and asserts RUNNING).
review.verdict: A careful, complete implementation of snapshot and restore across all three steps, with strong validation, documentation and tests. The only gaps are a minor clock-dependent edge case in wait snapshots, a flat snapshot type and one misnamed test.
